title: The Devi Gita
attributionNote: The tenth book of the Devi Bhagavata Purana and its philosophical climax, in which the Goddess herself teaches the king Himalaya on the mountain of the gods.
description: The Devi Gita presents the Goddess as the supreme reality and the world as her manifestation: she describes her own nature and the light of consciousness, the creation and dissolution of the worlds, the pilgrimage to her true seat, and the worship, breath-control and renunciation by which a devotee reaches her. It is the Shakta counterpart of the Bhagavad Gita.
historicalContext: Composed in Bengal within the Devi Bhagavata Purana, the Devi Gita gave Shaktism a philosophical scripture of its own, and it is studied today as the tradition's systematic account of the Goddess as Brahman.
availabilityNote: Complete: the ten chapters of the Sanskrit text as GRETIL publishes it, streamed from GRETIL at read time, one chapter at a time. This is the original Sanskrit, not a translation.
